clue.text: Senior Roman forced to make reparation

indicators.note: forced suggests letters pushed out of their natural order, so the word that follows is rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly Roman dignitary is compelled to pay compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' signals an anagram of REPARATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A praetor was a senior Roman magistrate, and the Praetorian Guard served the emperor; the word describes such a high-ranking Roman.

clue.text: Settle for an old measure of land

definitions.meaning: to settle or alight, as a bird on a branch
a rod or pole, five and a half yards, or a square of that side

explanation.definitionFit: A bird perches when it settles; a perch is also an old unit of length and area.

clue.text: Right up to the top in music

definitions.text: Right up to the top in music

parts.words: Right up to the top in music
parts.note: an Italian musical term for the very highest register

explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian term for 'very high' marks the highest octave or register.

clue.text: James's people at St James's?

definitions.meaning: envoys accredited to the Court of St James's, the British royal court

explanation.walkthrough: The Court of St James's is the formal name of the British royal court, to which foreign envoys are sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James's novel title names diplomats, who are formally accredited to the Court of St James's.

clue.text: Sailors TV producers often chase

definitions.meaning: audience figures that TV shows compete for

explanation.definitionFit: Ratings are non-officer sailors and also television audience figures.

clue.text: Formed up, having announced an attack

indicators.note: announced signals the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: Troops lined up after a raid was declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' signals that A RAID is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops arrayed are drawn up in formation, ordered in ranks.

clue.text: Beat wife and start to cheer

parts.note: the cheer 'hip hip hooray' starts with this word

explanation.surface: A domestic scene: a man beating his wife and then cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'start to cheer' is the opening word of 'hip hip hooray', not the first letter of 'cheer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip something is to beat it, either with a lash or, in cookery, a whisk.

clue.text: Tricked! Subatomic particle has no radius

indicators.note: has no means a letter is removed

parts.note: a hadron is a subatomic particle such as a proton

explanation.surface: A physicist exclaims at being fooled by a particle missing its radius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes R from HADRON.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had on is to be fooled or teased, a British idiom.

clue.text: A series of columns Priestley knocked out

indicators.note: knocked out suggests the name is knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: The playwright Priestley being floored by rows of pillars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' signals an anagram of PRIESTLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A peristyle is a row of columns surrounding a courtyard or building.

clue.text: Book burning — smoke holds up the perpetrator we're after

indicators.note: in a down clue holds up means one part sits above the parts below

parts.note: the culprit being hunted is 'our man'
a fire that is in is still burning
a Havana is a cigar, something to smoke

explanation.surface: A book-burning, with smoke sheltering the arsonist police are hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene's novel. 'holds up' places OUR MAN above IN HAVANA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Man in Havana is a 1958 novel by Graham Greene.

clue.text: Go back to buy yet another round?

definitions.meaning: stand treat again, buying more drinks

explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a backward withdrawal; split as re-treat it means paying for drinks once more.

clue.text: Game kept short as I'm not so slim

indicators.note: kept short means the game's name loses its last letter

parts.note: rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, similar to baseball

explanation.surface: A player complains a game was cut short because of their weight.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUNDERS is a British schoolyard bat-and-ball game rather like baseball; 'kept short' drops its final S. 'as I'm' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of round: someone more round in figure is plumper, the opposite of slim.

clue.text: There's no telling when you'll get this payment

definitions.text: There's no telling when you'll get this payment

parts.words: There's no telling when you'll get this payment
parts.note: 'no telling' seems to mean the timing is uncertain, but really the payment is for keeping quiet

explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to buy someone's silence is a bribe to stop them telling a secret.

clue.text: Less marshy at first across the pond

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word marshy

parts.note: across the pond, from a British view, means in America: IN US

explanation.surface: Someone notes that land is less boggy over in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' is British slang for the US, giving IN US.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic 'less' and this word both mean subtract, as in ten less two.

clue.text: Knife a god

parts.note: a shiv is slang for a knife, especially an improvised one

explanation.surface: An instruction to stab a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is one of the principal Hindu deities, the destroyer in the Trimurti.

clue.text: Boat given name, with helpful translation

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a boat
titled means given a name or title

explanation.surface: A newly named boat with an explanatory translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtitled film has translated text on screen to help viewers.

clue.text: Resent day being wasted sitting about

indicators.note: being wasted suggests the two words are wrecked and reformed into another

explanation.surface: Someone resents a day spent lazily lounging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being wasted' signals an anagram of RESENT DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes a life spent mostly seated and inactive.

clue.text: What sweetens a comfortless state: I do!

parts.note: Sparta was the austere Greek city-state
'Me!' is the eager reply to 'who does?'

explanation.surface: A claim to be the one bringing sweetness to a harsh place.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparta, the Greek city-state, is the byword for austerity.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial sweetener.

clue.text: Promote everything, including last of stock in kiosk

indicators.note: including means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to boost something is to promote it

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the word stock

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Advice to push every item on sale, including the final stock, in a small shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' tucks the final letter of 'stock' into the promote-and-everything pair; 'Promote' reads as a sales verb but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookstall is a small kiosk or stand selling books and newspapers.

clue.text: Merchant offering a pound off

parts.note: in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, the title merchant pledges a pound of his flesh to be cut off

explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is Shakespeare's merchant of Venice, who stakes a pound of flesh.

clue.text: Shot dead: turn off that camera!

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
'Cut!' is the director's call to stop filming

explanation.surface: A film director, after a shooting death, calls to stop filming.
explanation.walkthrough: A late cut is a cricket stroke played very late, steering the ball behind square on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a late cut is a stroke played as the ball passes the batsman.

clue.text: Sleep soundly in folded sheet

indicators.note: soundly here means as the word is pronounced, so a synonym for sleep is spoken

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps deeply wrapped in a folded bedsheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like a description of deep sleep but signals that the word is spoken: the geological term is pronounced like 'nap'.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology a nappe is a large sheet of rock folded and pushed over other strata.

clue.text: I cover over a set of books

indicators.note: over means the cover goes over and around the letter a

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Someone describes binding a set of volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts LID around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem is divided into twenty-four books, so it is literally a set of books.

clue.text: Stress wrong suit — clubs

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in an incorrect order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A card player stressed at following with the wrong suit in clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals an anagram of SUIT with C.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ictus is the rhythmic stress on a syllable.

clue.text: Fish good beat-here are three examples of one

definitions.text: here are three examples of one

parts.note: a tetra is a small tropical aquarium fish
to ram is to strike or beat hard

explanation.surface: A list of words followed by a puzzle-like remark about them.
explanation.walkthrough: The words Fish, good and beat each have four letters, so they are three examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is a four-letter word, and each of fish, good and beat qualifies.

clue.text: Author's workings around a line

indicators.note: around means the workings surround the line

parts.note: a mine is a set of underground workings
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A writer's mines wrap around a single line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L inside MINE. The 's in 'Author's' is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the writer of Winnie-the-Pooh.

clue.text: Not original article of this treaty?

parts.note: a later version is not the original one
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a clause in this treaty was added afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lateran Treaty of 1929 settled relations between Italy and the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran Treaty of 1929 established Vatican City; the name identifies that pact.

clue.text: Artist caught ugly woman completely

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hag is an ugly old woman
all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A painter is caught out by a thoroughly ugly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter famed for dreamlike pictures.

clue.text: Our mortal body, do you say?

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: the archaic form 'dost thou' means do you

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the human body's mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: DOST, the old form in 'dost thou', is said like the answer; the funeral service's 'dust to dust' supplies the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says we are made from dust and return to it, so the mortal body is called by that name.

clue.text: Conflict with bird tapping at door, in the story

indicators.note: in means the bird goes inside the story

parts.note: a conte is a short story, from French
in Poe's poem The Raven, the bird is heard tapping at the chamber door

explanation.surface: A tale has a bird at the door in a moment of conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe's poem has a raven 'gently rapping, rapping at my chamber door'; the French word for a short tale holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a rule is to go against it, to conflict with it.
